newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia central bank plans corporate bond programme.
newsitem.headline: Russia central bank plans corporate bond programme.

text.p: Russia's central bank is working on a corporate bond programme to be launched in autumn, the bank's Deputy Chairman Andrei Kozlov said on Monday.

"We are talking to a number of banks, who are in turn talking to their clients, to issue Treasury bill-like securities and to place the short-term paper in existing trading systems, including the Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange (MICEX), where they could draw funds to replenish their turnover capitals," Kozlov told Reuters.

The yields on government paper have fallen to about 20 percent from about 200 percent last summer, and banks, which used to hold a major part of their assets in government securities, are now looking at industry for investment.

"Now is the right moment for this -- there are enough funds, T-bill yields have fallen, they (T-bills) are no longer used as a speculative asset and market participants now feel a shortage of investment opportunities," Kozlov said.
He said the paper, which is likely to run for between three months and a year, would not be backed by the government, and the central bank would not participate in the market.
Foreigners will be allowed to participate in trading, he said.

Currently only one corporate bond, that of RAO Vysokoskorostnye Magistrali (VSM or High-Speed Railways in English), is traded on MICEX. The bond is backed by the government and the central bank acts as an agent.
